activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone.
Today I am going to explain an essential process that you regularly practise in Food Technology.
This process is controlling food temperature during preparation and storage.
Although it is a routine task, it must be carried out carefully and in the correct order, because incorrect temperatures can cause food spoilage and serious health risks.
First, you have to check the food storage temperature using a calibrated thermometer, because temperature control is critical for food safety.
Before handling any food items, the storage conditions should be verified.
Then, you have to identify the correct storage areas for raw and cooked items so that cross-contamination is avoided.
After that, you have to clean the thermometer probe to prevent contamination during checking.
Next, you have to record the initial temperature readings to create a clear reference point.
You shouldn’t start food preparation at this stage, because storage conditions must be confirmed first.
Proper preparation supports hygiene and safe handling.
Once preparation is complete, you have to monitor food temperature regularly during processing to ensure food is cooked or cooled safely.
The process should be observed carefully throughout cooking or cooling.
Then, you have to adjust heat levels when necessary, because uneven heating can leave food unsafe to consume.
After that, you have to stir or turn food as required so that heat is distributed evenly.
You also have to separate hot and cold food items to maintain correct temperature zones.
You shouldn’t rely on guesswork, because accurate readings are necessary for food safety.
Careful monitoring reduces contamination risks.
Finally, you have to check the final temperature before moving food to storage to confirm it is within safe limits.
Then, you have to label food containers clearly so that storage time can be tracked easily.
After that, you have to place food in the correct storage unit to maintain temperature stability.
You also have to clean and sanitise work areas to prepare for the next task.
You shouldn’t serve the food immediately, because proper cooling or holding time is required.
Following this sequence ensures safe and hygienic food handling.
